title: Godzilla Minus Zero opens to $31.6M, biggest North American opening for a live-action foreign-language film (AP); listed for Indian cinemas on 20 Nov
headline: Godzilla Minus Zero Tops North America With $31.6M Opening
caption:
Godzilla Minus Zero opened at No. 1 in North America with an estimated $31.6 million over 6–8 November. By AP's count, that is the biggest North American opening for a live-action foreign-language film, ahead of Zhang Yimou's Hero (2004). AP notes one exception if you count it: The Passion of the Christ, made largely in Aramaic, opened higher in 2004.

Takashi Yamazaki's sequel made about $63 million worldwide in its first weekend, $21.3 million of it on IMAX screens. Godzilla Minus One, which won the Visual Effects Oscar, opened at $11.4 million in North America in 2023.

Indian ticketing and trade listings put it in cinemas here on 20 November, with PVR INOX Pictures releasing it. Toho's own global release list doesn't include India yet. Sacnilk, Bollywood Hungama and The Week report the date moved from 6 November because of Ramayana's two-week hold on Indian IMAX screens.

Did you watch Godzilla Minus One in a cinema or at home?

Sources: AP, The Week, Dread Central, The Numbers, Sacnilk, Bollywood Hungama, District

alt_text: Slide 1: an official Toho International production still from Godzilla Minus Zero, under the headline "Godzilla Minus Zero Tops North America With $31.6M Opening". Slide 2: "No. 1", the biggest live-action foreign-language opening in North America: it ends Hero's 2004 record, per AP's count, and is nearly triple Minus One's $11.4M opening in 2023. Slide 3: "$63M" worldwide from its first weekend: IMAX screens made $21.3M of it, about a third; it follows Minus One, 2024's Visual Effects Oscar winner. Slide 4: "20 NOV", the listed date for Indian cinemas: ticketing and trade listings carry it, but Toho hasn't listed India; PVR INOX Pictures is releasing it here; it moved from 6 Nov, trade reports say.
